newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Mar palm oil output seen up 32 pct - Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Mar palm oil output seen up 32 pct - Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in March is expected to have risen by 32 percent to 663,000 tonnes from February, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Monday
Wong put palm oil stocks at end-March at 725,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 722,993 tonnes at end-February
Exports were estimated at 560,000 tonnes against February's 376,885 tonnes.
Wong said in a report that the roboust month-on-month increase was evident in all regions in the country.
He said the large increase in crude palm oil supplies coupled with a moderate drop in prices to more affordable levels had stimulated a strong recovery in demand in March.
The bulk of the increased exports was accounted by China which raised its offtake substantially to an estimated 115,000 tonnes from around 40,000 tonnes in February.
Wong said the inability of major competing oils to move decisively higher has tended to restrain the upward potential of palm oil even when the latter enjoyed a good pickup in demand.
Wong said with Indonesian exporters competing with Malaysian exporters in such major markets as China and India, prices are likely to face even greater difficulty to forge ahead in the coming weeks.
